3.0.s.en: 1. The setting up of a golden statue:

3.0.0.en: 1 "Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image of gold, whose height was threescore cubits, and the breadth thereof six cubits: he set it up in the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon. 2 Then Nebuchadnezzar the king sent to gather together the princes, the governors, and the captains, the judges, the treasurers, the counsellors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the image which Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up. 3 Then the princes, the governors, and captains, the judges, the treasurers, the counsellors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces, were gathered together unto the dedication of the image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up; and they stood before the image that Nebuchadnezzar had set up. 4 Then an herald cried aloud, To you it is commanded, O people, nations, and languages, 5 That at what time ye hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, ye fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king hath set up: 6 And whoso falleth not down and worshippeth shall the same hour be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace. 7 Therefore at that time, when all the people heard the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, and all kinds of musick, all the people, the nations, and the languages, fell down and worshipped the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up."

3.0.1.en: "Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image of gold, whose height was threescore cubits, and the breadth thereof six cubits: he set it up in the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon" [1].

3.0.2.en: Some rabbis see that Nebuchadnezzar wanted to erase the effect of the dream upon the people throughout his kingdom, for he felt that many had glorified the God of Israel; therefore he set up this statue to occupy people's minds. Was this statue of Nebuchadnezzar himself, to set himself among the ranks of the gods, or of the god Bel, the chief god of the state, or of a new god? The prophet Daniel does not mention it. But the prevailing opinion is that he wanted to deify himself. For though he had humbled himself for a while before the prophet Daniel, love of vain glory and pride quickly rose up in him.

3.0.3.en: Perhaps after the matter of his dream spread, the king feared that the Jews would incite the nations not to worship the king's gods; so the king set up this statue as a test for all the peoples he had taken captive, whether they were subject to him and to his worship or not. He set it up in the plain of Dura, or in the open city.

3.0.4.en: Because of the enormous size of the statue, some critics thought the story was not historical. But the reply to this is that it is not necessary that the whole statue be of pure gold, but only overlaid with gold, and that the dimensions of the statue include the massive base on which the statue stood.

3.0.5.en: "Then Nebuchadnezzar the king sent to gather together the princes, the governors, and the captains, the judges, the treasurers, the counsellors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the image which Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up.

3.0.6.en: Then the princes, the governors, and captains, the judges, the treasurers, the counsellors, the sheriffs, and all the wise men of the provinces, were gathered together unto the dedication of the image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up; and they stood before the image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up. Then an herald cried aloud,

3.0.7.en: To you it is commanded, O people, nations, and languages, that at what time ye hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, ye fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king hath set up:

3.0.8.en: and whoso falleth not down and worshippeth shall the same hour be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace.

3.1.0.en: Therefore at that time, when all the people heard the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, and all kinds of musick, all the people, the nations, and the languages, fell down and worshipped the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up" [2-7].

3.1.1.en: The dimensions of the statue pointed to deficiency, for we know that the number 7 points to perfection, while the number 8 points to what is beyond temporal perfection (because time is made up of the 7 days of the week), as though the number 8 meant the transcending of time, and the Lord Christ rose on the first day of the new week, or the eighth of the previous week. The number 6, however, points to deficiency; therefore the name of the Antichrist is 666 (Rev 13:13-18), that is, certain deficiency. And the statue here was sixty cubits in height and six cubits in breadth [1].

3.1.2.en: Nebuchadnezzar used every means so that all would worship his statue. He used the army, with the great men advancing at the head of the ranks to terrify the common people, and he used every kind of music of that time to stir the emotions. So in every generation the enemy of good uses every means to draw us into worshipping him by one means or another, or to turn men aside to the way of sin, and to count the holy life a life of rebellion against society.

3.1.3.en: The peoples bowed down to the statue, whether it was of Bel or of the king or of another god, not in a spirit of piety but by the command of the king, who threatened not only with death but with torture, where the disobedient would be cast into a furnace of fire.

3.2.s.en: 2. A complaint against the three youths:

3.2.0.en: The wicked spoke to the king with flattery and hypocrisy, ascribing to the faithful and godly youths ingratitude and disobedience toward the king and his commands, but the youths had learned that God must be obeyed rather than men (Acts 5:29).

3.2.1.en: "8 Wherefore at that time certain Chaldeans came near, and accused the Jews. 9 They spake and said to the king Nebuchadnezzar,

3.2.2.en: O king, live for ever. 10 Thou, O king, hast made a decree, that every man that shall hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, and dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, shall fall down and worship the golden image: 11 And whoso falleth not down and worshippeth, that he should be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace. 12 There are certain Jews whom thou hast set over the affairs of the province of Babylon, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego;

3.2.3.en: these men, O king, have not regarded thee:

3.2.4.en: they serve not thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up." [8-12].

3.2.5.en: Note here the use of some Greek musical instruments, for Greek culture had influenced the region through the spread of Greek merchants and the presence of Greek colonies before the rise of the Greek Empire.

3.2.6.en: It is clear from the text that the movements of the youths were under strict watch, especially after the command to worship the statue was issued. Perhaps some of the king's counselors told him that these men of foreign race did not join the rest of the men of the palace in the Babylonian religious rites, these whom the king had raised from slavery to occupy great positions in the state. Because of envy, the accusation was made against these godly men that they were ungrateful, rebellious, and not worshippers of the gods.

3.2.7.en: We should not wonder that the Chaldeans, whom Daniel and his three companions had rescued from certain death (Dan 2:2), came to the king complaining against those who had saved them, so that he might cast the three youths into the furnace of fire, thus repaying them love with hatred, and kindness with envy and a desire to be rid of them. For ingratitude is the nature of fallen man, and persecution is the mark of the wicked; they trouble the righteous without cause.

3.2.8.en: St. Clement of Rome says: [You find nowhere in the Holy Scriptures that the righteous were cast out by the holy. Truly we find in them righteous men persecuted by the wicked, good men imprisoned by the wretched, and just men stoned by the lawless and killed by men under wrath, who bore them envy and spite; but they bore such sufferings with glory. What shall I say, brethren? Was Daniel cast into the lions' den by men who feared God?! Were Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael cast into the furnace of fire by men who worshipped the Most High in a glorious and great manner?! Far be it from us to have this thought!].

3.3.0.en: "13 Then Nebuchadnezzar in his rage and fury commanded to bring Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. Then they brought these men before the king. 14 Nebuchadnezzar spake and said unto them, Is it of purpose, O Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that ye do not serve my gods, nor worship the golden image which I have set up? 15 Now if ye be ready that at what time ye hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, and dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, ye fall down and worship the image which I have made; well: but if ye worship not, ye shall be cast the same hour into the midst of a burning fiery furnace; and who is that God that shall deliver you out of my hands? 16 Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, answered and said to the king, O Nebuchadnezzar, we are not careful to answer thee in this matter. 17 If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king. 18 But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up."

3.3.1.en: "Then Nebuchadnezzar in his rage and fury commanded to bring Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.

3.3.2.en: Then they brought these men before the king.

3.3.3.en: Nebuchadnezzar spake and said unto them,

3.3.4.en: Is it of purpose, O Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that ye do not serve my gods, nor worship the golden image which I have set up?

3.3.5.en: Now if ye be ready that at what time ye hear the sound of the cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, and dulcimer, and all kinds of musick, ye fall down and worship the image which I have made; well:

3.3.6.en: but if ye worship not, ye shall be cast the same hour into the midst of a burning fiery furnace;

3.3.7.en: and who is that God that shall deliver you out of my hands?" [13-15].

3.3.8.en: Nothing provokes those in authority like the feeling that their authority is despised. They demand that all obey their commands even if they are unjust.

3.3.9.en: Having calmed a little, he gave them a last chance to save their lives, if they would bow down to the statue just once!

3.3.10.en: What concerned him was not whether they bowed to the statue or not, but their defiance of his authority; therefore he mocked their God, saying that He could not deliver them out of his hand.

3.3.11.en: "Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, answered and said to the king,

3.3.12.en: O Nebuchadnezzar, we are not careful to answer thee in this matter.

3.3.13.en: If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king.

3.4.0.en: But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up" [16-18].

3.4.1.en: The scholar Tertullian speaks of obedience to kings and rulers (Rom 13:1; 1 Pet 2:13-14) in everything except what touches the faith, saying: [For this reason also the three brethren were set forth as an example for us, who were obedient to Nebuchadnezzar in other matters, and with all firmness refused to honor the statue].

3.4.2.en: The youths could have found excuses by which to justify bowing down to the statue, among them:

3.4.3.en: a. They were young in age, and captives.

3.4.4.en: b. They were under the authority of a violent king.

3.4.5.en: c. The king held absolute authority, especially over them as prisoners of war. They were asked to bow down even once without being prevented from worshipping God.

3.4.6.en: d. Every kind of music was offered to influence them.

3.4.7.en: e. The king himself, who had granted them the blessings in which they lived in the palace, entered into the dialogue with them and began to threaten them.

3.4.8.en: f. They were in a foreign land, easily exposed to accusation. And in exile how easy it is to apply the saying: "When in Rome do as the Romans do."

3.4.9.en: g. Their forefathers in Jerusalem and all Judah and Israel worshipped idols even inside the very temple of the Lord, as is stated in Jeremiah and Ezekiel, and without external pressure, whereas these strangers insisted not to bow down to a statue in a foreign land.

3.4.10.en: h. By refusing to bow down to idols they were exposed to death, and so would lose every opportunity to play any part in working on behalf of their people. This is a purely human measure, which the young men rejected in a spirit of faith, trusting in God who works for their good and is able to deliver them if He so wills.

3.4.11.en: The furnace was of red brick, with an opening at the top, and it also had a side door through which the king saw the youths and with them the one like the son of the gods.

3.4.12.en: In the dialogue King Nebuchadnezzar challenged their God, while they defied death for the sake of their faithfulness to God. They believed that their God is able to save them, and if He did not save them from the temporal fire, this did not mean their betrayal of Him. They did not care about the king's threats, relying in their perseverance upon their living faith:

3.4.13.en: a. They believed that God is able to save them, and that He is the guardian of their lives, and that He would not permit their death if that were of benefit to them.

3.4.14.en: b. They believed that if He permitted them to die, they would accept it with courage, offering their lives as a sacrifice of love to God.

3.4.15.en: By this these youths are counted martyrs, because they bore witness to the divine truth, offering their lives as the price of witness, regardless of whether they were killed or the Lord rescued them from death. As St. Augustine says, martyrdom is not accomplished by the means of death, but by the state of the believer. For martyrdom rests on two principles: the first is faith in God as the keeper of our life and its leader to where He wishes, and the second is the opening of a door in heaven before our eyes so that we may see the glory prepared for us, looking upon our life here as a temporary passing.

3.4.16.en: * Look at their faith! They say: We believe that He is able to save us, but if our sins prevent Him, we believe in Him who does not wish to hand us over (to eternal death). We do not believe in this life but in the life to come. And we do not believe in Him so that we may escape burning here, but so that we may not escape passing through this fire and fall into another fire. So do what you wish, prepare your furnace, with this heat of it and its fire, for it is for our purification.

3.4.17.en: St. Jerome Perhaps some will ask: Why was no complaint made against Daniel that he did not bow down to the statue?

3.4.19.en: First: Perhaps Daniel was on a mission outside the region.

3.4.20.en: Second: Perhaps the accusers feared that the king would stand against them, because they knew his esteem for Daniel and how he had bowed down to him; therefore they wanted to focus on the three youths as Daniel's helpers, and perhaps it was in their plan to accuse him after being rid of these youths.

3.4.21.en: Third: Perhaps this was not demanded of Daniel, because the king felt that he himself ought to bow down to Daniel, for he is greater than the statue or on its level.

3.5.s.en: 4. The casting of the youths into the furnace:

3.5.0.en: "19 Then was Nebuchadnezzar full of fury, and the form of his visage was changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego: therefore he spake, and commanded that they should heat the furnace one seven times more than it was wont to be heated. 20 And he commanded the most mighty men that were in his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, and to cast them into the burning fiery furnace. 21 Then these men were bound in their coats, their hosen, and their hats, and their other garments, and were cast into the midst of the burning fiery furnace. 22 Therefore because the king's commandment was urgent, and the furnace exceeding hot, the flame of the fire slew those men that took up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. 23 And these three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell down bound into the midst of the burning fiery furnace." [19-23].

3.5.1.en: They were cast into the furnace from the upper opening.

3.5.2.en: By looking to the eternal fire they did not fear the temporal fire, nor dread death (Lk 12:4-5). For what did the fires of persecution do to them?

3.5.3.en: a. The Word of God appeared (like the son of the gods), He who was within them, appeared to embrace and protect them.

3.5.4.en: b. The flames loosed the bonds, but could not touch a hair of their body or the edge of their garment.

3.6.0.en: c. The king acknowledged their God, the Savior of His believers, and honored them in the province of Babylon [30].

3.6.1.en: St. John Cassian sees that the king of Babylon here signifies Satan, who stirs up within us the furnace of the fire of passions through gluttony.

3.6.2.en: * Being kept by this zeal of mind and continual contrition, we strike the dangerous passions of the flesh by depriving it (of the foods that stir it toward arrogance and pride); and thus by the abundance of our tears and the weeping of our hearts we succeed in quenching the flame of the furnace of our flesh, which the Babylonian king kindles (Dan 3:6), and which he continually feeds with occasions of sin and destructive vices. In this, by the grace of God, the dew can descend into our hearts by His Spirit, and the heat of the fleshly passions can be completely destroyed.

3.7.0.en: "24 Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonied, and rose up in haste, and spake, and said unto his counsellors,

3.7.1.en: Did not we cast three men bound into the midst of the fire?

3.7.2.en: They answered and said unto the king, True, O king. 25 He answered and said, Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the form of the fourth is like the Son of God. 26 Then Nebuchadnezzar came near to the mouth of the burning fiery furnace, and spake, and said,

3.7.3.en: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, ye servants of the most high God, come forth, and come hither.

3.7.4.en: Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, came forth of the midst of the fire. 27 And the princes, governors, and captains, and the king's counsellors, being gathered together, saw these men, upon whose bodies the fire had no power, nor was an hair of their head singed, neither were their coats changed, nor the smell of fire had passed on them. 28 Then Nebuchadnezzar spake, and said,

3.7.5.en: Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who hath sent his angel, and delivered his servants that trusted in him, and have changed the king's word, and yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god, except their own God. 29 Therefore I make a decree, That every people, nation, and language, which speak any thing amiss against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, shall be cut in pieces, and their houses shall be made a dunghill: because there is no other God that can deliver after this sort. 30 Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, in the province of Babylon." [24-30].

3.7.6.en: The furnace had a side door, at which the king stood at a distance to see them as they were cast in, one after another, and to watch them burning. But what did he see?

3.7.7.en: First: The flames proved them righteous in the eyes of God and the eyes of the king, and one like the Son of God appeared, glorifying them.

3.7.8.en: Second: The flames loosed the iron bonds and did not affect the clothes of the youths.

3.7.9.en: Third: While some of the soldiers who cast the youths in died because of the intensity of the heat, the youths were walking about.

3.7.10.en: Fourth: The flames turned into dew, and perhaps the king longed to enjoy what they were enjoying, but he could not enter in to them, but only called them to come out to him.

3.7.11.en: The youths did not come out of the furnace but kept walking about, until the command came to them from the king. They are obedient to him in the Lord.

3.7.12.en: The Chaldeans knew the story of the casting of the three youths into the furnace. They became a living witness, in the provinces of Babylon before all, of God the Savior of His godly ones and of the power of taking refuge in Him. But what did the king do regarding his eternity?!

3.7.13.en: * (By prayer) Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael were found worthy to be heard, and to be fortified by the blowing of a wind that brought dew and prevented the effect of the flame of the fire upon them. And the mouths of the lions in the den of the Babylonians were stopped by the prayers of Daniel.

3.7.14.en: * Hananiah and his companions went down into a spiritual blessing granted to all the saints, which Isaac pronounced when he said to Jacob: "Therefore God give thee of the dew of heaven" (Gen 27:28), greater than the physical dew that quenched the flame of Nebuchadnezzar?!

3.7.15.en: * Now too Nebuchadnezzar speaks the same words as ours, for we are the true Hebrews, Hebrews of the life to come (Heb 11:13); we experience the heavenly dew that quenches all fires from us, and with the same higher side of our souls we imitate these youths.

3.7.16.en: Origen * Truly prayer was used in the ancient world to be freed from fires (Dan 3), from beasts (Dan 6), and from famine (1 Kgs 18; Jas 5:17-18); and yet it had not received its form from Christ. How much greater, then, is the work of Christian prayer?!

3.7.17.en: Tertullian * These three youths became an example for all believers, for they did not fear the crowd of governors, nor were they terrified at hearing the king's words, nor did they shrink when they saw the flame of the furnace glowing, but counted all men and the whole world as nothing, keeping the fear of God alone before their eyes.

3.7.18.en: If Daniel stood far off in silence, yet he encouraged them to be joyful and good, and smiled at them. Indeed he himself rejoiced for the witness they bore, and for the understanding that had come to them as it had come to him, so that the three youths might receive the crown of victory over Satan.

3.7.19.en: * (The king) called the three youths by their names, but he did not find a name by which to call the fourth, for He had not yet (become incarnate) and become Jesus, born of the Virgin.

3.7.20.en: * They were honored not only by God but also by the king. They taught the foreign and alien nations to worship God.

3.7.21.en: St. Hippolytus of Rome * When the furnace was closed upon them, the flames fled, the blaze gave refreshment, and the Lord was present with them, affirming that no power stands against those who confess Him and His martyrs, for those who trust in God receive no harm, but are always safe from dangers.

3.7.22.en: * They added that God is able to do all things, but they did not speak thus in order to seek temporal deliverance, but to enjoy the glory of eternal freedom and eternal security.

3.7.23.en: * By saying "But if not..." they let the king know that they were also able to die for the God whom they worship. For this is the power of courage and faith. And with faith, knowing God's power to rescue from present death does not mean fear of death nor flight from it. By this faith is proved with greater power.

3.7.24.en: * The three youths Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael were equal in age, united in love, steadfast in faith, persevering in virtue, stronger than the flame and the punishments laid upon them, declaring that they obey God alone, and know Him and worship Him alone.

3.7.25.en: St. Cyprian * The three holy youths showed themselves superior to the pleasures of lust, and despised the king's wrath, and were marked by courage without fear of the terrors of the furnace of fire that Nebuchadnezzar commanded to be kindled. They proved that the golden statue worshipped as a god is of no use...

3.7.26.en: * How did the three youths triumph over the power of fire? Was it not by perseverance?

3.7.27.en: St. Basil the Great * The three youths in Babylon became renowned through the flames.

3.7.28.en: St. Augustine The great men gathered, probably those who had complained against the youths, but before discussing the matter among themselves, perhaps to find what would justify their slander, the king issued his decree to destroy whoever stands against their God, offering them temporal honors as well. But he neither condemned idol worship nor abandoned it. He mixed his honoring of the living God with idol worship and its abominations. He did not care to ask about the One who was with the three youths in the furnace in order to be joined to Him and enjoy Him.

3.8.s.en: 6. The Song of the Three Youths:

3.8.0.en: Then the three began with one mouth to praise God and glorify Him and bless Him in the furnace. We will speak about this wonderful song, which the Church uses daily, when we speak about the deuterocanonical books, if the Lord wills.

3.8.1.en: * God is in His place even now, He is in our midst, He who of old made the fire of the furnace in Babylon cold.

3.8.2.en: St. Basil the Great * The three youths were righteous; they cried to the Lord while in the furnace, and as they praised, the fire became cold. The flame could not come near to harm the innocent and upright youths, since they praised God, and He saved them from the flame.

3.8.3.en: * It is clear that He did not forsake the three youths who praised in the furnace; the flames could not touch them.

3.8.5.en: Let me walk with You in the midst of the furnace!

3.8.6.en: * Let the fires be kindled, let the flame blaze, let the enemy roar, so long as You are within me I do not tremble!

3.8.8.en: Instead of groaning, let my life turn into a hymn of praise!

3.8.9.en: Be revealed in my depths, and be glorified in my weakness, O God of the impossible!

3.8.10.en: Reveal Yourself for the salvation of every human soul, O Savior of the world!

3.8.11.en: Grant me the spirit of prayer with praise, that I may defy through You the fires of affliction, and even the fires of the devil and his evil works!

3.8.12.en: I no longer fear even sin, for You are the giver of victory over it!
